simple: scale-up means more GPUs inside one computer; scale-out means more computers joined by a network.
analogy: more halls in the same building, joined by corridors; more buildings, joined by roads across town.
precise: scale-up communication runs between GPUs of one node over PCIe or GPU-to-GPU links (NVLink, xGMI); scale-out communication runs between nodes over network cards (Ethernet with TCP, InfiniBand or RoCE with RDMA). The two have different alpha and beta and are combined in hierarchical algorithms.
source: C1 and D6 of BR-04 (Systems Curriculum Track F 14.1; PCIe and NVLink documents, title only) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); the split into two words is this university's usage

simple: a picture of the best speed a link can give you, for every message size.
analogy: a small parcel is limited by the time it takes to start a delivery; a full truck by the road's capacity.
precise: attainable bandwidth = min(beta, n / alpha) for a message of n bytes over a link with start-up time alpha and bandwidth beta; the two lines meet at the ridge n = alpha × beta, where the alpha-beta model n / (alpha + n / beta) gives exactly beta / 2. The roofline model with message size in place of arithmetic intensity.
source: D9 and D4 of BR-04 (Williams, Waterman, Patterson, roofline paper; Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp; title only) — pending verification; values computed by R1 of BR-04 (run in this build)

simple: measuring the same transfer at many sizes, from tiny to huge, instead of at one size.
analogy: timing a bowl, a pot and a full cart on the same road.
precise: a benchmark that times one operation for sizes spaced by a constant factor over the whole range a program uses, so that alpha (small end) and beta (large end) can both be read and the size where one dominates is visible; milestone F2 tests from 4 bytes to 1 GiB.
source: C1 of BR-04 (Systems Curriculum, milestones F1 and F2, quoted); R3 and R5 of BR-04 (runs in this build)

simple: the members of a group job do not make the same group calls in the same order.
analogy: half the table passes bowls of soup while the other half passes bowls of salad.
precise: an erroneous program in which the ranks of a communicator call collectives in different orders or with non-matching arguments (count, type, root, operation); the MPI Standard requires matching calls, and the outcome otherwise is not defined (in BR-04's run: memory corruption in two ranks, then a hang).
source: D2 of BR-04 (MPI Standard, collective communication chapter, title only) — pending verification; R9 of BR-04 (run in this build)
